skill.name: flow-tdd
skill.description: Guides AI coding agents through strict test-first development, failure verification, minimal implementation, refactoring, and error logging.
skill.summary: Enforces a strict red-green-refactor workflow for AI-assisted development.
skill.author: Dimon94

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, regex examples, and repository-relative links. One semantic risk remains: the skill tells agents to delete implementation code when TDD was not followed. No evidence of hidden command execution, network access, credential access, or prompt injection was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before deleting or commenting out implementation code. Prefer a branch, backup, stash, or review note first.
Tell agents to ask before running project test commands when dependencies or scripts are untrusted.
Package referenced guidance with the skill or describe the needed context without parent-directory links.

static_findings.snippet: **Root Cause**: 正则表达式 `/^.+@.+$/` 过于宽松,接受了 `user@` 这样的无效邮箱
**Resolution**: 更新正则为 `/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/` 要求至少有域名和顶级域

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Code Deletion Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends deleting implementation code when tests were not written first. This can cause an agent to remove user work without explicit confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guidance directly recommends deletion as the preferred response to code written before tests. The risk is clear because an agent could apply it to user files.

content.value_statement: Teams lose confidence when code is written before tests and failures are not tracked. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through strict TDD steps with failure checks and error logs.
actual_capabilities: Defines a red, green, refactor workflow for test-first development.
Requires new tests to fail before implementation begins.
Guides minimal implementation one passing test at a time.
Defines quality rules for behavior-focused, independent, fast tests.
Provides an ERROR_LOG.md workflow for test and build failures.
Cross-references flow-dev constitution and attention refresh materials.
limitations: Does not include scripts or tooling to enforce TDD automatically.
Relies on the agent and user to run project-specific test commands.
Does not define language-specific test frameworks or commands.
Includes deletion guidance that should require user confirmation.

use_cases.title: Add a Feature with TDD
use_cases.description: Use the skill to write a failing test, implement the smallest fix, and refactor only after tests pass.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Coding Discipline
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to verify that an AI coding session followed test-first development.

use_cases.title: Track Test and Build Failures
use_cases.description: Use the error logging workflow to capture failures, root causes, resolutions, and prevention notes.

prompt_templates.title: Start TDD for a Small Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a narrow feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-tdd for this change. First write one failing test, show the failure result, then implement the smallest passing change.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Existing Work to TDD
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request when code exists before tests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use flow-tdd to recover test-first discipline for this existing change. Propose a non-destructive plan before changing or removing any code.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Test Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these tests using flow-tdd quality rules. Identify tests that pass without proving behavior, then propose stronger failing tests.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full TDD Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply flow-tdd across red, green, and refactor phases for this requirement. Record each failure, implementation step, and cleanup decision.

output_examples.input: Add validation for invalid email addresses using flow-tdd.
output_examples.output: The agent first proposes a failing validation test, confirms why it should fail, then adds the minimal validation behavior.
The agent records the phase, failure type, message summary, root cause, resolution, and prevention note in the error log.

output_examples.input: Existing implementation was written before tests.
output_examples.output: The agent asks for confirmation before any destructive cleanup and offers a non-destructive test-first recovery plan.

best_practices: Ask the agent to show the failing test result before implementation.
Keep implementation scoped to one failing behavior at a time.
Review destructive cleanup steps before code is removed.
anti_patterns: Writing production code before a failing test exists.
Accepting tests that pass immediately without investigation.
Treating broad refactors as part of the green step.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It tells the agent to run project tests, but the project environment supplies the actual command.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include language-specific testing advice?
faq.answer: No. It describes a general TDD workflow and expects the user or project to choose the test framework.

faq.question: What should happen if a new test passes immediately?
faq.answer: The skill treats that as an invalid test or evidence that implementation already exists.

faq.question: Does it modify project files?
faq.answer: It instructs the agent to create or update ERROR_LOG.md when failures happen. Confirm file changes before applying them.

faq.question: What is the main safety concern?
faq.answer: The skill recommends deleting code to restore TDD discipline. Agents should ask before removing user work.
